A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FaCT-GS and contain readable main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite repagination and the added appendix study.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction, runtime, scalability, initialization, and compression experiments, including appendix warm-start and Gaussian-count studies.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical studies and adds component-level acceleration experiments in Appendix A and Table 3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.6 retain the same initialization strategies, rasterization and voxelization procedures, acceleration components, optimization objectives, and volume fitting. The new appendix evaluates existing components by disabling them; it does not revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: The reconstruction datasets, multiresolution Coral data, paired initialization volumes, RPLHR-CT warm-start cases, and compression tasks are retained. The new acceleration ablation reuses the existing 75-view benchmark and 50-view 2k Coral scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding reconstruction, scaling, initialization, and compression experiments retain their comparator sets. Table 1 still evaluates FDK, SIRT, FISTA, IntraTomo, NAF, and R2-Gaussian. X-field is newly cited but not evaluated; the new timing comparisons are internal component ablations.

E3.justification: V2 adds experiments individually reverting acceleration components in two retained scenarios, using an RTX 4070 and an LS40 GPU, respectively, as named in Appendix A. These are additional ablation protocols; the original benchmark settings, metrics, sample counts, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A systematically isolates fused TV/SSIM, voxelizer and rasterizer acceleration, bounding boxes, and the per-Gaussian backward pass across two scenarios. This substantially extends analysis of which components produce the speedup beyond v1's aggregate kernel measurements. Existing warm-start and Gaussian-count analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run/seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added timing ablation continues point-estimate reporting without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Under unchanged stated settings, Table 1 revises FaCT-GS's 75-view PSNR/SSIM from 38.80/0.949 to 39.05/0.950, placing PSNR above R2-Gaussian's unchanged 39.04. New Table 3 reports component timings, including rasterizer-reversion penalties of 359 s and 3568 s. Other matched benchmark, compression, warm-start, and qualitative results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the Gaussian representation, rasterization expressions, losses, normalized iteration ratio, and relative SSIM definition. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: fast scalable reconstruction, over 4× and 13× speedups, volumetric warm starts, and compact Gaussian representations. The additional ablation supports these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly explains the dominant contribution of the per-Gaussian backward pass and the smaller voxelizer/TV gains through their fixed 32-cubed regions. Section 5 explicitly frames volume fitting as a compression proxy. Section 6 removes the qualification that downstream Gaussian analysis has not yet been demonstrated for CT.

D1.justification: V2 documents hardware and component reversions for the new ablation and redirects code/data access information from the repository to a project webpage. Existing implementation settings remain unchanged, and data availability was already stated in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds X-field to the CT related-work discussion and reference list and more explicitly acknowledges inspiration from prior Gaussian Splatting acceleration in the introduction. The additional R2-Gaussian bibliography entry duplicates an existing work rather than expanding research coverage.

P1.justification: Local edits revise the abstract/introduction, reorganize compression explanations between Sections 5–6, and extend acknowledgements. The new Appendix A shifts the retained appendices to B–D. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds the acceleration-ablation Table 3 and renumbers the retained warm-start table as Table 4. Existing displays are retained with some resizing and relocation, and Table 1 updates its PSNR ranking colors. The overall visual structure remains similar.

improvement.justification: Appendix A and Table 3 strengthen the central runtime contribution by identifying which optimizations drive the speedup, addressing a gap in v1's aggregate timing evidence. The gain is limited because the method and most validation remain unchanged. Clearer compression framing helps, although removing the explicit CT-specific caveat makes downstream applicability less carefully qualified.
